solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Parrot about to stuff mouth (5)

indicators.note: you stuff something by packing a filling inside it, so CA is packed into the mouth

blocks.note: a maw is an animal's mouth

explanation.surface: Someone feeds a talkative parrot, stuffing its mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: About sounds like a direction to go around; here it is the abbreviation for circa, and it is the filling, not the wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large long-tailed parrot of Central and South America, so parrot defines it by its family.

clue.text: Romeo’s friend met Curio after tense exchanges with Romeo (8)

indicators.note: the letters of met Curio are taken as they stand once the swap has been made, so after sets the order of operations
to exchange places with someone is to swap positions, so T and R trade places

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean friend runs into a character called Curio, then trades barbs with Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: In METCURIO the T and the R swap places. Curio is also a Shakespeare character, which helps the disguise, and Romeo does double duty on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercutio is Romeo's witty friend in Romeo and Juliet, so the definition names him by his role in the play.

clue.text: Shell in vehicle shifting quickly (8)

explanation.surface: A shell rattles around inside a fast-moving vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Shell could be petrol or ammunition here; it is the hard casing of a crab or tortoise.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a turtle or crustacean, the zoologist's word for that shell.

clue.text: Something covering features with a crude humourless act (6,9)

indicators.note: something crude is roughly put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disguise, a mask perhaps, worn for an unfunny, vulgar performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is W plus A plus HUMOURLESS ACT; crude sits in the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus moustache is a thick drooping one that hides the mouth, so it covers facial features.

clue.text: Member of defence regularly saw what overlooked claims could be? (9)

blocks.note: a defender in football or rugby
to date someone is to see them regularly

explanation.surface: A defender kept an eye on something missed in a list of claims.
explanation.walkthrough: Regularly looks like an alternate-letters signal on saw; it is part of the phrase for going out with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim that was overlooked might be backdated to the time it should have been paid.

clue.text: Snubbed robust complaint (4)

indicators.note: a snub nose is short at the end, so snubbed means the last letter is cut

explanation.surface: A strong objection was brushed aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Snubbed reads as ignored; here it clips the tail of BEEFY.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal slang for a grievance, as in what's your beef?

clue.text: Meeting company with head lacking in deduction (10)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and it is missing

explanation.surface: A company meeting where the boss is not up to reasoning things out.
explanation.walkthrough: Head in a business surface suggests a chief; here it is the first letter of INFERENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a conference is a formal meeting for discussion.

clue.text: Regional administrators instruct codicil should be changed (8,7)

indicators.note: the letters are to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Local officials order that an addition to a will be amended.
explanation.walkthrough: A codicil is an addendum to a will, which gives the legal surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A district council is an elected body running a local area, so its members administer a region.

clue.text: Warder missing northern country (6)

indicators.note: a warder missing N is one without that letter, as a coat missing a button lacks it

blocks.note: an old word for a jailer

explanation.surface: A prison guard is absent from a country in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: A turnkey held the keys in an old prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is a country spanning Europe and Asia, defined by example.

clue.text: Leave cornered, pulled up after partial loss of power (6)

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting it turns it the other way
only part of the letters for power, one P of two, go

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a corner retreats after the electricity partly fails.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing TRAPPED gives DEPPART, which has two Ps; losing one of them is the partial loss of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to depart is to leave, as trains depart a station.

clue.text: Cleric managed to nab retiring journalist on Russian river (5,4)

indicators.note: to catch and hold, so the other pieces go inside
retiring means withdrawing, drawing back, so the journalist is read backwards

explanation.surface: A clergyman arrests a shy reporter beside a river in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: Retiring reads as shy in the surface; it is the backwards signal. The journalist sits after the river, so on means placed next to.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural dean is a Church of England cleric overseeing a group of parishes.

clue.text: Band splits after going west (5)

indicators.note: an across answer read westward runs right to left

explanation.surface: A pop group breaks up after moving west.
explanation.walkthrough: Band suggests musicians; it is a strip of material.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a strip of leather or fabric, the non-musical sense of band.

clue.text: Reverse hype? Relax (6)

blocks.note: the prefix that undoes an action
a plug is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A plea to stop the hype and chill out.
explanation.walkthrough: Unplugging is taken as undoing a plug, with UN- doing the undoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unplug is an informal idiom for switching off from work and unwinding.

clue.text: This speaker approves two tries (4,4)

indicators.note: two tries means the word for tries is written twice

blocks.note: a judge hears, or tries, a case

explanation.surface: A speaker nods through a couple of attempts.
explanation.walkthrough: Tries means attempts in the surface; in court, to try a case is to hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hear hear is what a listener calls out in a debate to approve a point.

clue.text: Duke’s gushing, not upset (10)

indicators.note: in a down answer, turned upside down reverses it

explanation.surface: A duke is effusive but not upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke’s means Duke is; upset reads as unhappy but turns NOT over.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Wellington defeated Napoleon at Waterloo, so the title alone points to him.

clue.text: Corrupt eminent cop; extremely cocky example of uselessness (12)

indicators.note: something corrupted is spoiled, so the letters are rearranged
only the extremes, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A senior officer on the take, and arrogant with it, is hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: Only EMINENT COP is rearranged; CY is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Incompetency is the state of being useless at a job, so any instance of it is an example of uselessness.

clue.text: Naval location cut short, over 0.9144m (8)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits above the next

blocks.note: to dock a tail is to cut it short

explanation.surface: A naval site cut back by just under a metre.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd number is simply a yard in metric.
explanation.definitionFit: A dockyard is where naval ships are built and repaired, defined by where it is found.

clue.text: Lloyd set fancy typeface (3,5)

indicators.note: elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Lloyd chose an ornate font.
explanation.walkthrough: Set belongs to the fodder, though it looks like a typesetting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Style is a family of serif typefaces.

clue.text: Local left in charge of small hospital in trendy teaching institution (6,6)

indicators.note: hospital in trendy means the H is placed inside the word for trendy

blocks.note: the local is your nearest pub

explanation.surface: The pub left a small hospital in charge of a fashionable college.
explanation.walkthrough: The local is British for your usual pub. A British public school is, confusingly, a private fee-paying school.
explanation.definitionFit: A public school in Britain is an independent fee-paying school, a kind of teaching institution.

clue.text: Shocked judge took flight having lost billions (6)

indicators.note: something that has lost a letter no longer has it, so B is dropped

explanation.surface: A judge ran off in alarm after losing billions.
explanation.walkthrough: B for billions comes off BOLTED; the surface makes it sound like a financial scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to be jolted is to be given a sudden shock.

clue.text: Arm functioning after electronic hand shackles withdrawn (6)

indicators.note: to shackle is to hold captive, so the hand holds E inside
drawn back, so read backwards
functioning comes after the rest in the answer

blocks.note: a paw is a hand, reversed to WAP

explanation.surface: A limb working again after an electronic tag on the hand is taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: Arm reads as a limb in the surface; it is a noun meaning a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms are weapons, as in the arms trade, so one arm is one weapon.

clue.text: Deliberate individual nuance (8)

explanation.surface: A pondering of a person's subtle shade of meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliberate reads as a verb, to ponder; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is a subtle additional sense, the same shade of meaning as a nuance.

clue.text: Shakes “a kilo” in brief search (6)

indicators.note: a kilo in the search means those letters sit inside it
a brief thing is cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A quick hunt turns up a quivering kilo of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks just bundle a kilo as one piece; K is the kilo abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something that quakes shakes or trembles.

clue.text: A round American fruit (4)

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it

blocks.note: as in ten pounds a head, per head

explanation.surface: A round fruit from America.
explanation.walkthrough: A looks like the letter A; it is PER, which wraps round A for American.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: pears are an orchard crop grown for eating, one kind among many.

clue.text: Matter of huge imaginary circle having radius cut (5)

indicators.note: having the radius cut means it is taken out of the circle

blocks.note: a line of latitude round the globe
the r of geometry formulas, removed

explanation.surface: A geometry question about a vast circle with a shortened radius.
explanation.walkthrough: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are imaginary circles round the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the topic is the subject matter under discussion.

clue.text: Article, risqué, about old Conservative form of government (9)

explanation.surface: A saucy newspaper piece about a Tory government of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: About only means concerning here: RACY comes after the O and C it is about.
explanation.definitionFit: Theocracy is government by priests in the name of God, one form of government among many.

clue.text: Screw undone, ergo nearly out (9)

indicators.note: not quite all, so the last letter goes
put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loose screw, so it must be almost out.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is British slang for a prison warder, which a dungeoner is.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeoner is a jailer, and screw is slang for a prison officer.

clue.text: Organ essentially protected by vein implant (5)

indicators.note: at its essence, the middle letter
surrounded by another piece

explanation.surface: A heart or kidney is carefully stitched into a vein during a transplant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is surgical, but vein is a seam of ore and implant is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge something is to fix it firmly in place, the same sense as implanting it.
